refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: These configuration files control report TSA timestamping. See systemd.syntax7 for a general description of the syntax.

refsect1.title: Options
refsect1.para: The following settings are configured in the [TSA] section:

listitem.para: The URL of the RFC 3161 Time Stamping Authority to contact. The digest of the report is submitted to this endpoint as an HTTP POST request, and the signed timestamp token returned by the authority is attached to the report.

Note that many public TSA endpoints are plain HTTP rather than HTTPS. This is normal for RFC 3161: the returned token is cryptographically signed, hence transport confidentiality is not required for its validity.
The maximum time to wait for the Time Stamping Authority to answer. If the authority does not respond within this time, signing fails.
Takes a time span value. The default unit is seconds, but other units may be specified, see systemd.time7. Defaults to 30 seconds.

Takes an absolute path to a PEM file containing one or more certificate authority certificates. These are used as the trust anchors when validating the signing certificate of the timestamp token returned by the Time Stamping Authority. When set, the system-wide trust store is not consulted, hence only authorities chaining to the listed certificates are accepted. This is primarily useful for private or corporate Time Stamping Authorities whose certificates do not chain to a publicly trusted root.
Note that this setting governs validation of the timestamp token only; it has no effect on TLS peer verification of the connection to the authority, which always uses the system-wide trust store.
If unset, the system-wide trust store is used.
